chapter: Chez Florence, the Hot Club and Django
title: Chez Florence, Florence and Palmer Jones's cabaret
summary: Entertainers Florence and Palmer Jones opened Chez Florence at 61 Rue Pigalle with a staff of entertaining musicians; it faded after Palmer Jones's mysterious death and Bricktop took over.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: So he brought Florence Jones, and Palmer Jones, and the entertainers, they went over like a house on fire.
Briggs
Well, Louie, poor Louie, the race course meant him no good at all. He finally -- didn't go broke, but he borrowed money from a lady who had a hotel on the Rue Pigalle.
And she, this person, Mrs. Regina, had an idea of getting Mitchell, and his wife, to open a cabaret in her place, that's why she --
I see.
That's why she loaned him such money, and then she pulled out, and when she pulled out he was bankrupt, so he was forced to go to work for her.
I see.
He and his wife, went to 61 Rue Pigalle. Rue Blanche. 61 Rue Pigalle, which became Chez Florence.
I see. I see.
Florence Jones. A wonderful entertainer, she certainly was,
Briggs

and so was he, pianist and entertainer. He was what you would call, one of the society entertainers in America that you could -- they'd send for him all over the States, you know. They'd pay any price for him.
And he opened up the Chez Florence with Palmer Jones and Florence Jones, the Chez Florence.
Right.
And, he, in turn, engaged certain musicians like Harvey White, the drummer, and a wonderful singer. 'Cause he based it on entertaining, you see.
Right.
And music was just a second line for them. They played dance music, I mean, but it was just one of those things, you see.
The basis was entertainment. They had Sammy Richardson, Opal Cooper, --
Right.
Briggs
You heard of him?
Yes.
I saw Opal before he died, in '74.
And we had Louie Jones, who became a professor at the Howard University.
Really.
'Cause he was studying while we were playing, at Chez Florence, he used to play saxophone, but his real instrument was violin. He was studying at the Conservatoire in Paris.
Oh, I see.
I met him when we came here. He's a personal friend of mine.
And Louie Jones and that's about all and then Brashear. You know Brashear was of the AA finally.
Brashear finally joined that outfit at Chez Florence, which was after he left Cricket Smith.
And, they finally had all Paris
Briggs

at their feet, you know, just one of those things.

They had the entertainment business in their hands. And they did very, very well, until unfortunately one morning, we heard -- I wasn't here, I was in Chamonix, a casino in Chamonix, but I heard -- had a letter saying that Palmer had died. Palmer Jones had died. And I think he had -- I don't know, it was a mysterious death.
Right, right.
Mysterious death, in a cabaret or something, after hours, you see.
I see.
And, well, Chez Florence then started to fade, when Palmer -- 'cause Palmer was really the basis of everything. And that's where Bricktop came in.
She came in at that point?
Briggs
She came in, and it was taken over.
